ecard2_printing_phenomenon: Pokemon-e Dot Code variants. Aquapolis issued four cards (Golduck 50, Drowzee 74, Mr. Mime 95, Porygon 103) in two physical prints each, distinguished only by the e-Reader dot code data — and, on Mr. Mime alone, by one clause of Poke-Body wording. Artwork and illustrator are identical across each a/b pair. No un-suffixed print of these four numbers exists, so ATTR-0's 'lone' classification is correct rather than a modelling gap. Unrelated to the Yellow A Alternate mechanism.

f16_bounding.generalised_cross_set_duplicate_test: every one of the 37 suffix-variant printings across all 218 TCGdex sets was tested for a same-local_id counterpart in a different set; exactly 12 rows matched — the 6 xya rows and their 6 set-scoped twins — and no other suffix variant in the catalog has any cross-set counterpart
f16_bounding.population_re_derivation: 37 suffix variants / 23 with base / 14 lone, re-derived independently from all 218 sets on 2026-08-20; identical to ATTR-0 §5 and to Gate 1 production A-5

repair_population_effect: unchanged. All 6 xya rows are CONFIRMED_CORRECT and must not be repaired. The ATTR-1 repair population remains exactly the 12 rows confirmed by ATTR-0 and Gate 2.
post_repair_convergence: repairing g1-28a to Ryo Ueda and xy9-107a to Naoki Saito makes all six xya/twin pairs agree on illustrator, eliminating both F-16 attribution contradictions. F-16 then degrades from an attribution-correctness problem to a pure catalog duplicate-identity problem.
incidental_observations: All six xya rows carry no image asset upstream (image = null) while all six twins do — the xya rows are metadata-only duplicates. Recorded for a later image/coverage slice; IMG-0 not started.

The xya set carries no logo and no symbol, and a releaseDate of 2014-02-05 inherited from the XY series rather than the May 2017 – November 2020 Yellow A Alternate window — further evidence it is a synthetic provider grouping, not a physical expansion.

Card names differ cosmetically across three of the six pairs (e.g. 'Zygarde EX' vs 'Zygarde-EX'), so any future dedup keyed on name equality would fail on half the pairs. Recorded for F-16 design, not acted on.
catalog_completeness_follow_up: 79 (Bulbapedia Yellow A Alternate, May 2017 – November 2020) vs 37 (catalog suffix variants) discrepancy re-confirmed and explicitly NOT resolved here. ATTR-0b produced no evidence that it must be resolved before attribution repair: a printing absent from the catalog cannot carry a wrong attribution, so it cannot enlarge the confirmed-defect population. Remains a separate Catalog Trust / sync-coverage item.
gate_verdict_reason: all 14 canonical rows investigated at the exact-printing level with two agreeing sources each, zero unresolved; F-16 fully bounded at 6 duplicate pairs by a generalised cross-set test over the whole catalog; no new evidence class discovered; the confirmed repair population is unchanged at 12 rows
artifact_hash_note: SHA-256 over the LF-normalised UTF-8 bytes of the committed CSV. docs/attr-0-evidence/*.csv is pinned to eol=lf in .gitattributes, so the working-tree bytes match on every platform.
interpretation_limit: This gate verifies the ILLUSTRATOR CREDIT on each exact printing and the PHYSICAL PRINTING IDENTITY relationship between provider rows. It does not verify artist_id, aliases, or any Illustrated Vault resolution behaviour, it proposes no aliasing or deduplication mechanism, and it performs no repair. CAT-0 F-15 remains open and still blocks per-row repair.
